title: Louis, duc de Bourgogne → his brother Philip V of Spain, two letters partly in a number cipher whose key the editors could not find (353 numbers printed)
correspondents: Louis, duc de Bourgogne → Philip V, king of Spain
shelfmark: Autograph originals formerly in the archive at Alcalá de Henares (Baudrillart cites the duke's letters as 'Arch. d'Alcala, l. 2514'); now Archivo Histórico Nacional, Madrid, Estado (inference, not checked); printed Baudrillart and Lecestre, Lettres du duc de Bourgogne au roi d'Espagne Philippe V et à la reine, vol. 1 (Société de l'histoire de France, 1912), letters X and XI, pp. 21-22 and 26-27
folio_note: Letter X (21 Jan): 213 numbers in three runs (126, 64, 23) with short clear phrases between; letter XI (28 Jan): 140 numbers in two runs (109, 31). 353 numbers, 126 distinct values, range 1-406. Transcribed from the page images in bourgogne1703_ciphertext.txt in this folder (two independent readings, no difference).
status: Printed undeciphered. Editors, vol. 1 p. 19 note 1: 'Ce chiffre n'a pu être retrouvé ni aux archives du ministère des Affaires étrangères, ni à celles d'Alcala; heureusement le duc de Bourgogne ne s'en est servi que deux fois, le 21 et le 28 janvier 1703.' p. 21 note 1: 'on ne peut donner la traduction en clair de cette lettre chiffrée.' p. 26 note 2 refers back. The duke sent Philip the key himself with his letter of 7 Jan 1703 ('Je vous envoie ce que je vous ai promis ... Vous y trouverez de toutes sortes de choses'). Volume 2 (1916) and Baudrillart, Philippe V et la cour de France vol. 1 (1890) searched for 'chiffr' and 'clef': no key, no decipherment. Tests run, all FAILED (details in the README): four French keys of 1690-1703 (Louis XIV's code of 1690/93 as far as published, the petit chiffre of Pignerol 1690-91, the Grand Chiffre of 1691, the Bonac-Groffey key R639) applied unchanged miss, while each passes its own control; the counts fit a syllable-and-word nomenclator of about 300 entries rather than a letter cipher, and a ciphertext-only attack calibrated on synthetic text of the same length failed 0 of 5, so none was run on the real text. Not on DECODE as far as known.py shows.
why: The only cipher in the private correspondence of Louis XIV's grandson with the new king of Spain at the start of the War of the Spanish Succession, in a key the duke made himself for things 'qu'il ne seroit pas prudent d'écrire en clair'.
score_note: Scored from the printed pages, read on the page images, during the printed-editions sweep of 16-17 Nov 2026 (research/sweep_2026-11-17_ajbeling_printed_editions/); the autographs not seen
verify: Ask the Archivo Histórico Nacional (Estado; Alcalá legajo 2514 in Baudrillart's citations) for the letters of 21 and 28 Jan 1703 (an interlinear decipherment by Philip V or a secretary?) and for the key sent with the letter of 7 Jan 1703 (also legajo 2460, Louis XIV's letters to Philip).

title: Count Willem Frederik of Nassau-Dietz → Prince William II of Orange, number cipher in three letters; the passage of 27 Feb 1650 printed bare and called 'non déchiffré' by the editor
correspondents: Willem Frederik, count of Nassau-Dietz, stadholder of Friesland → William II, prince of Orange
shelfmark: Koninklijk Huisarchief, The Hague (inference: Groen's source, not stated on the pages read); printed Groen van Prinsterer, Archives ou correspondance inédite de la maison d'Orange-Nassau, 2e série, t. IV (1859), letters DCCCCXXXVII, DCCCCXLIV and DCCCCL, pp. 336-337, 344-346, 353-354
folio_note: 133 numbers in the three letters: 102 in a low range (1-83, and 200), apparently letters, 30 code numbers 91-143 and one '1050'; letter groups 'AO. BE.' and 'F. K. M. [L.]' in 950. Letters 937 and 944 are printed with readings set above the numbers (a partial decipherment, several readings plainly wrong); 950, about 29 cipher words in 8 runs, has none.
status: Introduction p. xlvii: 'Dans la Lettre 950 un passage non déchiffré' (probably on the same subject as 937 and 944: Amsterdam). The editor glosses only 115 (de l'argent) and 118 (V. A.) in 950, carried over from the readings of 937 and 944. A partial key can be built from those readings (about 18 letter values and 9 code words); a held-out test of such a key on letter 937 FAILED (40% against a 70% mark, and its own control failed too), so no reading is offered. Related but different documents: catalogue 1982 (KHA letters to the counts of Nassau-Dietz, including Joachim Andreae's, 1645-53), lead 2715 (Hendrik Casimir I, 1640). Upstream's printed-series sweep downloaded the Groen volumes but records nothing for these letters.
why: Willem Frederik's secret correspondence with William II in the weeks before the Prince's attempt on Amsterdam (July 1650), the crisis of the first stadholderless period.
